candidates.exact_span: This permit may be reopened to establish effluent limitations for the parameter(s) to be consistent with that approved State standards in accordance with 40 CFR 122.44(d).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether this reopener is treated as establishing or potentially altering enforceable effluent limits during the permit term affects which numeric limits are applicable for compliance comparison (A) and whether monitoring tied to those limits is in scope (B).

candidates.exact_span: Additionally, language has been added stating that the permit may be reopened and modified during the life of the permit if relevant portions of the State WQS are revised or remanded.
candidates.computation_change_reason: If WQS revision or remand triggers permit modification, the operative limits and associated monitoring for the evaluation period may differ from those otherwise read from the static permit text (A, B).

candidates.exact_span: The permit may be reopened to include conditions of the completed TMDL.
candidates.computation_change_reason: TMDL-derived conditions introduced via reopening could add or change numeric effluent limits and monitoring obligations, altering which limit-measurement pairs and requirements are evaluated (A, B).

candidates.exact_span: Therefore, no additional requirements beyond the previously described technology-based or water quality-based effluent limitations and monitoring requirements, are established in the proposed permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of whether FY2025 obligations are confined to previously described TBEL/WQBEL limits and monitoring, versus additional proposed-permit requirements, changes the set of enforceable limits (A) and applicable monitoring duties (B).

candidates.exact_span: The limitations and monitoring requirements set forth in the proposed permit are developed from the State water quality standards and are protective of those designated uses.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether limits and monitoring are read as WQS-derived operative requirements versus narrative justification affects which numeric limits and monitoring conditions are treated as enforceable for the period (A, B).

candidates.exact_span: Effluent discharges flows are intermittent and are not directly discharged to Animas River.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Intermittent discharge and indirect routing to the receiving water bear on discharge-occurrence-dependent monitoring applicability (B) and on classifying periods without ordinary numeric results as no-discharge, conditionally excused, or unresolved (C).

candidates.exact_span: Facility flows described in the 2016 Statement of Basis were 0.181 MGD and have not increased (now 0.177 MGD as discussed above).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Stated flow magnitude and the claim that flows have not increased may affect applicability of flow-based or capacity-linked effluent limits and whether antibacksliding materiality exceptions apply (A).

candidates.exact_span: The permit requirements and the limits, including mercury, are protective of the receiving waters designated uses of that water consistent with 2020 Water Quality Management Plan and Continuing Planning Process (See Table 2-1. Tier Descriptions and Summary of Antidegradation Protection Requirements).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Reference to mercury limits and antidegradation tier protection via Table 2-1 affects which mercury numeric limit applies and whether compliance comparisons are enforceable versus narrative-only (A).

candidates.exact_span: interim or final effluent limitations must be as stringent as those in the previous permit, unless material and substantial alterations or additions to the permitted facility occurred after permit issuance which justify the application of a less stringent effluent limitation
candidates.computation_change_reason: Antibacksliding stringency and the material/substantial-alteration exception govern whether a proposed limit may be less stringent than the prior permit, changing which numeric limit is selected for comparison (A).

candidates.exact_span: The proposed permit maintains the permit requirements of the previous permit for TSS, TRC and pH.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Explicit carry-forward for TSS, TRC, and pH signals continuity of those limits and associated requirements, while implying other parameters may differ; misreading this span changes limit selection (A) and monitoring obligation continuity (B).
